Senses.PreferredTarget: take away the person, not the surroundings
AlternateTargets: person taken away, surroundings not taken away
remove the person but not the scene
Senses.Explanation: The first member of Linji's four statements later called the Four Selections: ‘at times, take away the person but not the surroundings.’ Linji's own record gives the complete set and then records the monk's question ‘what is taking away the person but not the surroundings?’ Linji answers, ‘the warming sun brings forth brocade spread over the ground; an infant's hanging hair is white as silk.’ The formula subsequently circulates as a verse heading and repeatable public question. Kefu's verse begins ‘its conditions themselves carry entangling error; if you try to seek the mysterious purport, deliberation instead reproaches you.’ Fengxue answers the inherited question with ‘a newly emerged red-furnace golden pellet strikes through the monk's iron face-door,’ while another later master answers ‘the home country has a road that no one reaches.’ These answer-lines are recorded deployments of the formula.
Senses.Note: 339 hits in the wave plan. Cross-read against all four members and the Four Selections (四料揀). The English keeps person (人) and surroundings or scene (境) literal. It is corpus-wide in later use: later verses and masters take up the same named question.

Senses.PreferredTarget: take away the situation, not the person
AlternateTargets: remove the surroundings, not the person
Senses.Explanation: The second member of Linji's “four selections” (四料揀): literally, “take away the situation, not the person.” Here “situation” (境) is the presented surroundings or objects, while “person” (人) is the person. Linji first enumerates four possibilities in an evening instruction: sometimes take away the person but not the situation; sometimes take away the situation but not the person; sometimes take away both; sometimes take away neither. In the recorded follow-up he answers this member with, “the king's command has already gone throughout the realm; the general beyond the frontier has ended smoke and dust” (王令已行天下遍，將軍塞外絕煙塵). Later masters retain the exact category but supply different answers: “secretly transmit the emperor's edict; double the journey by a hundred stages,” “build the altar and appoint the general,” “muddy head and earthy face,” or paired states such as “silent, silent; alert, alert.” The category is therefore a reusable public-interview question within Linji's fourfold roster, not a proposition whose intent this entry resolves. Its Zen deviation lies in the bureaucratic verb “take away” becoming one axis of a named appraisal scheme for person and presented situation.
Senses.Note: The allowlisted concordance has 404 matches in 145 texts. The retained evidence includes Linji's four-member enumeration, Linji's own transmitted answer, and three independent later question-and-answer deployments. Family revalidation against the “four selections” (四料揀), “take away the person, not the situation” (奪人不奪境), “take away both person and situation” (人境俱奪), and “take away neither person nor situation” (人境俱不奪) confirms that this is one roster member rather than an independent statement. Different answers are readings/deployments of the same category and must not be split under item 8. SenseKey remains null: Linji supplies the historical source, but the same category and meaning recur across later masters and texts, so historical origin does not make the sense master-specific.
